findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration dereferences [0] on a SELECT that returns no rows whenever no site_settings row named 'embed_category' has a value exactly matching a live category name — the case for every fresh install (site_settings is empty while migrations run) and every site that never set embed_category or whose named category was renamed/deleted — so execute(...)[0]['id'] raises and aborts the migration. db:migrate fails mid-upgrade (IndexError/NoMethodError on the empty result), blocking the upgrade entirely; the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback the author wrote is unreachable dead code because [0] raises before it can ever yield 0 — the same file guards its other lookup with cmd_tuples > 0 but leaves this one unguarded.

[BUG] The host-copy loop is guarded by `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`, but PG::Result#cmd_tuples reports rows affected by DML and is 0 for a SELECT (ntuples is the row count), so the guard can never pass. No embeddable hosts are ever copied from the old setting, and line 31 then deletes the 'embeddable_hosts' setting row — sites that used embedding silently lose all configured hosts at upgrade and embedding breaks with no error until an admin re-enters every host by hand.

[BUG] The INSERT interpolates each raw setting value without the scheme/path stripping the old allows_embeddable_host? applied and without the model's before_validation, so entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — both exercised as working values by the removed specs — are stored verbatim and can never match record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison. Upgraded sites whose working host entries carried a scheme or path end up with rows that authorize nothing (embedding silently denied for those hosts); a stored value containing a single quote additionally makes the INSERT raise a SQL syntax error that aborts the migration.

[BUG] update and destroy look up the host with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately dereference it, so a request for a nonexistent id raises NoMethodError (save_host(nil) / nil.destroy) and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any stale or hand-crafted PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id for an already-deleted record produces a 500 on the admin API.

[BUG] before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving an EmbeddableHost whose host is nil (e.g. POST /admin/embeddable_hosts with embeddable_host: {category_id: X} and no host key) raises NoMethodError inside the callback and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. The create/update endpoints crash with a 500 on a missing host field; the format validation never gets the chance to reject the request.

[BUG] The host validation regex accepts a ':port' suffix, but record_for_host matches only uri.host, which excludes the port, so a host saved as 'example.com:8080' passes validation and can never authorize any referer. Admins can save port-qualified hosts that appear configured but always fail the embed check with 'invalid referer host' — a silent misconfiguration; the old setting matcher stripped ports via URI(h).host, so port-carrying entries that worked before the migration stop working.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex requires a dotted domain with an alphabetic TLD, rejecting IP literals and single-label names like 'localhost' that the old setting matcher accepted (URI(h).host rescue h compared them directly against the referer host). A migrated IP or single-label host keeps working until an admin edits it — then even a category-only change fails validation with no way to re-save, and such hosts can never be re-added via the UI or API.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the relocated category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators. Specs still pass because Fabrication loads the whole directory, but the next contributor adding or editing a category fabricator opens category_fabricator.rb and finds the embeddable-host fabricator; the feature also needlessly rewrites a file it doesn't own.

[ADVISORY] update re-renders the embedding without persisting anything, and its only client caller, saveChanges() in admin-embedding.js.es6, sends update({}) and is wired to no template control. PUT /customize/embedding is dead surface: anyone who later wires a save button gets an endpoint that looks like a save path but silently no-ops.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the embeddable-hosts gate with no replacement, and the rewritten spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes trivially because a built topic has has_topic_embed? == false and embed_truncate defaults to false. After an admin deletes all hosts, previously imported topics remain expandable where the old blank-setting behavior disabled expansion site-wide, and no test in the diff exercises any host-related condition for this method.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable now issues a database query (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? → WHERE lower(host) = ?) on every embed request, replacing an in-memory cached SiteSetting check, and host has no index (which lower(host) would defeat anyway). Every iframe embed request — externally embedded pages, often a site's highest-traffic surface — pays a new per-request sequential scan that the previous implementation served from memory.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts class inheritance; create, update and destroy — including save_host's blank-category → uncategorized_category_id fallback — have no behavioral assertions anywhere in the diff. The endpoints' contract (param shape, serialization, the uncategorized fallback, the 500s on missing ids) ships unverified, so regressions in the headline 'edit category/host relationships' flow land silently.

[ADVISORY] belongs_to :category has no dependent cleanup and the migration creates no foreign key, so destroying a category leaves embeddable_hosts.category_id dangling. Imports from that host then pass a dead category_id to PostCreator and the admin hosts table renders a blank category badge for the orphaned row.

[ADVISORY] delete() chains destroyRecord().then(...) without the .catch(popupAjaxError) that save() uses. A failed destroy (e.g. the host was already removed by another admin) fails silently with an unhandled rejection and no error popup, while save() errors are surfaced.

[ADVISORY] There is no uniqueness validation on host, and record_for_host resolves duplicates with an unordered .first. Two rows for the same host with different categories make the category assigned to newly imported topics depend on database row order rather than admin intent.

[ADVISORY] The new plural _ids branch maps every id through _lookupSubType and assigns the result unconditionally, dropping the falsy guard the singular branch keeps (if (hydrated)), so an id with no matching side-loaded record becomes an undefined entry inside the hydrated collection instead of being skipped. A payload whose *_ids reference a record absent from the side-load yields collections containing undefined, which blow up when iterated in templates — the singular path's guard exists precisely because the lookup can return falsy.

[ADVISORY] No migration spec exists anywhere in the diff (the test-shaped files are limited to spec/controllers, spec/fabricators, spec/models and test/javascripts) for a migration that rewrites site configuration and deletes the source setting rows. A regression in the setting-parsing or category-mapping SQL corrupts or drops hosts at upgrade time with no safety net — the exact class of failure this migration already exhibits.

[BUG] CreateEmbeddableHosts indexes row 0 of two query results with no emptiness guard (lines 11 and 15), so on any site without an `embed_category` row in site_settings — the common case, and every fresh install where migrations run before seeds — the first lookup returns zero rows and the migration raises (PG::Result#[] IndexError or a nil dereference on ['id']), aborting db:migrate. Upgrades fail for the majority of existing forums (those that never configured embed_category) and fresh installs cannot migrate at all; the author's own third query guards with cmd_tuples, showing the unguarded lookups are the oversight, and admins must hand-patch the migration to proceed.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting values verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so legacy entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' — which the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? matched via URI(h).host and the deleted site_setting_spec cases explicitly exercised — are stored un-normalized. record_for_host compares lower(host) = URI(host).host exactly, so those migrated rows never match and embedding from those hosts silently starts returning InvalidAccess after upgrade (imports fall to Uncategorized); the new specs mask this because they build hosts through the model, which normalizes them.

[BUG] The INSERT statement interpolates the legacy setting value directly into SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), and the old setting was unvalidated free text. Any legacy host value containing an apostrophe raises a SQL syntax error that aborts the upgrade mid-migration, and the interpolated value is otherwise injectable into the statement (admin-controlled input, so primarily a robustness failure).

[BUG] update and destroy fetch the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and dereference it without a nil check (lines 10-11 and 15-16). Saving or deleting a host that another admin (or a stale tab) already deleted raises NoMethodError inside save_host/destroy and returns a 500 instead of the 404 the REST contract implies.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update re-renders the current embedding without reading params or persisting anything, and the client saveChanges action that targets it (embedding.update({}) in admin-embedding.js.es6) is referenced by no template. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 with unchanged state — untraceable scaffolding (route + action + client action) that gives any future caller a silent false-success while discarding their changes.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation on host and the migration creates no unique index, so duplicate rows for the same host are storable through the new UI and API. record_for_host resolves matches with an unordered .first, so when duplicates disagree on category_id the category applied to imported topics is arbitrary — an admin editing one duplicate row's category can see no effect while the other row governs.

[ADVISORY] Validation accepts hosts the matcher can never resolve: the format regex permits uppercase and an optional :port while before_validation only strips scheme/path, but record_for_host matches lower(host) against URI#host, which is lowercase and port-less. An admin saves 'MySite.COM' or 'example.com:8080', gets a success response, and embedding from that host remains denied with no feedback that the entry is dead.

[ADVISORY] The diff swaps the contents of the two fabricator files: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the four category fabricators were moved into the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The next contributor editing category fabricators opens category_fabricator.rb and finds an embeddable-host fabricator; re-adding Fabricator(:category) to its canonical home collides with the stray definition (Fabrication duplicate error), so a routine future change breaks the suite.

[ADVISORY] The for_digest spec hunks (removing the unused `topic =` local at lines 1241 and 1249) are unrelated cleanup with no traceable connection to the embedding feature. Unrelated changes ride in an embedding PR — reviewers must audit them, and blame for digest specs points at an embedding commit.

[ADVISORY] The plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded unconditionally deletes every `*_ids` key from hydrated payloads app-wide and replaces it with a hydrated association, unlike the singular branch which preserves the key when hydration fails. Any existing or future client code reading a `*_ids` property off a store-hydrated object loses the attribute silently; this app-wide invariant change is tested only against the new fruit/color fixtures.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable runs on every embedded-comments request and now resolves permission through a SQL query (`lower(host) = ?`, line 17) with no index on host, replacing the previous in-memory site-setting read. The embed hot path (per pageview of embedded comment iframes, plus TopicRetriever and TopicEmbed.import) pays a non-indexable sequential scan per request where the old path was a cached memory lookup.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import assigns the topic's category solely from the embed URL's host record with no fallback (line 42: `category: eh.try(:category_id)`), whereas the removed embed_category setting applied to every import. Any import path not preceded by a host check — feed-polling imports being the notable one — silently lands in Uncategorized instead of the previously configured category.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test asserts a condition the implementation no longer reads — expandable_first_post? no longer consults embeddable hosts at all. The test passes vacuously (embed_truncate defaults to false and the built topic has no embed), giving false confidence that host-blankness is enforced and covering nothing about the changed code.

[ADVISORY] delete() calls destroyRecord without a .catch(popupAjaxError), unlike save() one action above. A failed delete (network error, 403) closes the confirm dialog and leaves the row in place with no error surfaced to the admin.

[ADVISORY] embeddable_hosts.category_id has no foreign key and EmbeddableHost declares belongs_to :category with no cleanup path, so deleting a category leaves host rows pointing at it. Imports for those hosts then run with a stale category_id (no longer the admin's intended category) and the host row renders a blank category badge, with nothing prompting the admin to fix the mapping.

[BUG] The migration backfills each legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting line verbatim via raw SQL INSERT, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (strip scheme/path), so entries the old `allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly matched via its URI branch (e.g. `http://discourse.org`, `https://example.com/1234`) are stored in a form `record_for_host` can never match. After deploy, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false for every previously-working referer whose stored setting entry carried a scheme or path, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess and embedded comments 403 site-wide on those installs; the new specs never catch it because they create hosts through Fabricate, which normalizes. Recovery requires an admin to manually re-save every host.

[BUG] `record_for_host` lowercases the stored column (`lower(host) = ?`) but binds `uri.host` un-downcased, and Ruby's URI preserves host case, so the comparison is case-sensitive against a half-normalized parameter. A referer whose host contains any uppercase character (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/page`) never matches an all-lowercase stored host — the common case — so `ensure_embeddable` rejects the embed with InvalidAccess and `TopicEmbed.import` falls back to no category; the `lower()` on one side expresses case-insensitive intent the query does not deliver.

[BUG] `embeddable_hosts.host` has no UNIQUE index (and the model adds no uniqueness validation), so the schema permits two rows for the same host with conflicting `category_id` values. An admin can add the same host twice (double-submit or plain error) with different categories; `record_for_host`'s unordered `.first` then picks an arbitrary row, so imported topics land in an unpredictable category and the admin grid shows contradictory duplicate rows.

[BUG] `belongs_to :category` is declared with no FK in the migration and no `has_many :embeddable_hosts, dependent: ...` on Category, so deleting the category leaves `embeddable_hosts.category_id` dangling. After an admin deletes the category a host points at, the row survives with a dead category_id: the admin grid renders a blank category badge, and `TopicEmbed.import` passes the nonexistent id to PostCreator for every import from that host.

[BUG] The validation regex caps the TLD at `[a-z]{2,5}` and requires a dot, so valid hosts with TLDs longer than 5 characters and dotless intranet hostnames are unrepresentable. Admins cannot add legitimate embed sources like `example.technology`, `example.capital`, or `myserver` (all of which the old free-text setting accepted), and the save is rejected with a validation error that looks like a bug in the new UI.

[BUG] The before_validation callback dereferences `self.host` with `sub!` while the model has no presence validation, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. A POST/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts whose `embeddable_host` payload omits the `:host` key assigns nil and crashes in the callback, returning a 500 instead of the 4xx validation error the contract implies.

[ADVISORY] `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` re-renders the serializer without persisting anything, so the advertised PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that returns 200 while discarding its payload. The only client caller, `saveChanges()` in admin-embedding.js.es6 (`this.get('embedding').update({})`), is wired to no button in embedding.hbs, so the entire embedding-level save path is dead on the client and a silent no-op on the server — the next person wiring a save button inherits an endpoint that loses data while appearing to succeed.

[ADVISORY] `ensure_embeddable` now issues a `lower(host)` table lookup on every embed request where the old path read the in-memory cached site setting, and no index on `host` backs the non-sargable predicate. Every embedded-page view (comments/count endpoints) pays a DB round-trip plus a sequential scan that was previously a memory read; on a high-traffic forum with many embedded iframes this is a per-request query added to a hot path for a lookup that changes only when an admin edits hosts.

[ADVISORY] The new plural branch of `_hydrateEmbedded` drops the truthiness guard the singular branch has: it maps ids through `_lookupSubType` without checking each result and deletes the raw `*_ids` key unconditionally (and a null `*_ids` value throws TypeError on `.map`). Any payload whose `*_ids` reference a subtype or id that fails to hydrate is silently rewritten from raw ids to an array containing `undefined` — data the singular path deliberately preserves — breaking the next consumer that reads the ids or rendering broken rows on the embedding grid.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator definitions are swapped between files: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all four `:category` variants (the new file's blob a37f5b4c8ba is exactly the old category_fabricator.rb content). Tests still pass because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but the next person adding a category variant edits the obvious file and finds an embeddable_host fabricator there, or redefines `:category` and collides with the existing definition in the wrongly-named file.

[ADVISORY] `expandable_first_post?` silently drops the embeddable-hosts conjunct entirely (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`), removing the global kill-switch the old `embeddable_hosts.present?` check provided. An admin who deletes all hosts to disable embedding no longer stops first-post expansion for previously imported topics; the renamed spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes vacuously (embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is false on a built topic), so no guard pins the old semantics.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex's `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` group accepts `host:port` entries, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host` with the port stripped, so a stored port-qualified host can never match any referer. An admin who enters `example.com:8080` gets a green saved row that silently allows nothing (the lookup compares `lower(host) = 'example.com'` against the stored `example.com:8080`), with no feedback that the entry is dead configuration.

[ADVISORY] The save success handler re-derives the category from local state (`Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`) instead of using the serialized host returned by the server, which is the component that applies the blank-to-uncategorized fallback. When an admin clears the category chooser and saves, the server stores `uncategorized_category_id` but the row renders a blank category badge (findById(null) is undefined) until the next full page reload, and the discarded response already contained the correct value.

[BUG] The category lookup `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` raises an exception when the SELECT returns no rows, so the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback is unreachable dead code and db:migrate aborts. Any upgrading site whose `embed_category` setting is unset, blank (the default is ''), or does not exactly match an existing category name gets zero rows from the JOIN; `execute(...)[0]` then raises (IndexError on the PG::Result the code itself relies on via `cmd_tuples` at line 19, or NoMethodError on nil), crashing the migration and blocking the upgrade for the majority of sites instead of falling back to the uncategorized category as intended.

[BUG] The migration inserts the raw site-setting strings (e.g. 'http://discourse.org', 'https://example.com/1234') via SQL without the model's before_validation normalization, so rows are persisted with scheme and path intact. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares against `URI(referer).host` ('discourse.org'), so every migrated host entry that used the scheme/path formats the deleted SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported (the removed site_setting_spec 'works with a http host' test proves such values existed) silently stops matching after upgrade — those sites' embedded comments begin raising InvalidAccess with no error shown to the admin.

[BUG] The INSERT statement interpolates `#{h}` directly into SQL with no escaping or parameter binding. A stored `embeddable_hosts` value containing a single quote (the old setting accepted arbitrary text with no validation) produces a SQL syntax error that crashes db:migrate and blocks the upgrade; the value is also concatenated into SQL unescaped.

[BUG] record_for_host compares the port-less `uri.host` of the referer against the stored host, but the validation regex on line 2 accepts and persists port-qualified hosts like 'example.com:8080'. An admin who adds 'example.com:8080' — accepted by the regex and matched by the old allows_embeddable_host? (which parsed each configured entry with URI(h).host, stripping the port, as shown in the deleted site_setting.rb code) — gets a database row that can never match any referer, so embedding from that host silently fails with 'invalid referer host' while the admin UI lists it as an allowed host.

[BUG] The contents of category_fabricator.rb and the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all four category fabricators. Specs still pass only because Fabrication loads every file in spec/fabricators regardless of filename; any future edit to category fabricators will be attempted in category_fabricator.rb, which no longer contains them, and the file layout contradicts its own name — an accidental mutation of existing files, not a deliberate reorganization.

[BUG] update and destroy fetch the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` with no nil check. A PUT or DELETE for an id that no longer exists (e.g. a second admin deleted the host while the first was editing it, or a stale API call) raises NoMethodError on nil inside save_host (`nil.host=`) or on `nil.destroy` and returns a 500 instead of a 404.

[BUG] save_host dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without guarding against a missing payload, and EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` without guarding against a nil host. A create/update request with no `embeddable_host` key crashes with NoMethodError (`nil[:host]`), and a request with `host: null` crashes in before_validation (`nil.sub!`), both returning a 500 instead of the 4xx validation error the JSON contract implies.

[ADVISORY] The retained test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer exercises any host-related condition: the implementation silently dropped the hosts-configured precondition from expandable_first_post?, and the test now passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false and has_topic_embed? is false on an unsaved topic. A semantic change (first-post expansion no longer requires any configured embeddable host, altering behavior for sites with embed_truncate enabled but zero hosts) ships without an explicit acceptance decision, and the misleadingly-named test provides false coverage — it would still pass if the method regressed or if the embed_truncate default ever flipped.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges() calls `embedding.update({})` but no template in this diff invokes the action, and the server-side PUT /customize/embedding (Admin::EmbeddingController#update) persists nothing — it only re-renders the serializer output. A save affordance that does nothing ships in the client controller, and an admin API endpoint returns 200 with serialized data without writing anything; anyone wiring up a save button later or trusting the PUT endpoint gets a silent no-op.

[ADVISORY] The delete action calls destroyRecord() with no .catch(popupAjaxError), unlike the save action which does handle failures. When the DELETE request fails (server error, expired session), the rejection is unhandled: no error dialog appears and the row silently remains in the table, leaving the admin unsure whether the host was actually removed.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex is much narrower than the free-text setting it replaces: it rejects IP addresses, dot-less internal hostnames, underscores, and TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. '.museum', '.travel'). Admins upgrading from the old setting — whose parser accepted any of these formats (URI(h).host rescue nil || h fell back to raw comparison) — cannot re-enter such hosts in the new UI at all, so embedding from those hosts becomes impossible to configure, with only a generic validation error as feedback.

[BUG] The migration interpolates the stored `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value unescaped into a SQL INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), turning admin-set configuration data into raw SQL. The old `embeddable_hosts` setting was free-text (`host_list`) that accepted arbitrary strings (the removed code even tolerated full URLs like 'http://eviltrout.com'), so any stored value containing a single quote aborts the upgrade with a SQL syntax error, and a crafted stored value executes arbitrary SQL with full database privileges during migration — the config-backed-sink threat model treats this admin/API-writable setting as attacker-controllable input.

[ADVISORY] `ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which executes an uncached `SELECT ... WHERE lower(host) = ?` query on every request, replacing the previous in-memory cached site-setting comparison. Forums with heavy embedding traffic gain one database round-trip per embedded pageview on /embed/comments and /embed/count — a path that previously cost zero queries — and `lower(host) = ?` cannot use a plain index on host (the new migration creates none), so the lookup is always a sequential scan; under embed-traffic spikes this adds measurable database load.

[BUG] The only spec for the new CRUD controller asserts class inheritance (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`) and never issues a request, so create/update/destroy and save_host are completely unverified (evidence-of-absence: this diff's only other controller specs are the identical subclass check in embedding_controller_spec.rb and the embed_controller specs, none of which touch this controller). Real defects ship green: `update`/`destroy` with an unknown id (e.g., a second admin deleting from a stale page) hit `save_host(nil)`/`nil.destroy` → NoMethodError → 500 instead of 404; `params[:embeddable_host]` missing → NoMethodError → 500; and the core feature behavior — `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` and the render_json_error validation path — has zero coverage, so any regression in the category-assignment logic this PR is about lands undetected.

[BUG] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddingController asserts subclassing; no test ever requests show or update, so the suite passes regardless of what those actions do. The controller's actual behavior — including that `update` persists nothing (see the no-op PUT finding) — can never fail this spec; a regression in fetch_embedding or the serializer wiring would also land green.

[BUG] `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a copy of `show`: it reads no params and persists nothing, yet routes.rb registers it as `put "customize/embedding"` and admin-embedding.js.es6's `saveChanges()` (`this.get('embedding').update({})`) targets exactly this endpoint. Any caller of PUT /admin/customize/embedding (the wired saveChanges action or an API consumer) gets a 200 with the unchanged payload and no indication that nothing was saved; the vacuous subclass spec is the only test, so nothing can catch it.

[BUG] `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host` without downcasing the bind value, and Ruby's URI preserves host case, so `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?('http://EvilTrout.com')` returns false even though 'eviltrout.com' is an allowed host — and the new spec (spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb:26-30) only exercises all-lowercase inputs, so the mirror-test table never hits the case the code mishandles. Embed requests whose Referer header contains any uppercase character are rejected with Discourse::InvalidAccess, and TopicEmbed.import assigns no category, for correctly-configured sites; the half-case-insensitive lookup ships with a test suite that structurally cannot detect it.

[BUG] The fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb (lines 1-27) defines the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators (confirmed by the blob hashes — the new file's hash equals category_fabricator.rb's old hash). The host fabricator lives in an unrelated file and the category fabricators no longer live where every contributor looks for them; tests only keep passing because Fabricator eagerly loads every file in spec/fabricators, so the next person editing category fixtures edits the wrong file and the mismatch spreads.

[BUG] The new plural branch maps every id through `_lookupSubType` and unconditionally `delete obj[k]`, so an id absent from the side-loaded collection produces `[undefined]` in the hydrated association and destroys the raw ids — the singular branch deliberately guards this case with `if (hydrated)` — and no test in the diff covers a missing reference (store-test.js.es6 only pins the all-references-resolve happy path). A payload referencing a missing side-loaded object (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids` containing a since-deleted host's id) yields undefined entries in `embedding.embeddable_hosts` with the raw ids unrecoverable, and the `hydrated || []` dead code shows the falsy case was never actually handled or tested.

[ADVISORY] Beyond the plural support, this diff also adds `delete obj[k]` to the pre-existing singular branch (the old code kept both `obj[subType]` and the raw `*_id` key), changing hydration semantics for every embedded `_id` key app-wide, and no test pins the new semantics — the store tests assert the hydrated association but never the raw key's presence or absence. Any existing client code reading `model.get('category_id')`/`farmer_id` after a fetch now silently gets undefined; since this is shared infrastructure used by every rest-serializer payload, the unpinned behavior change is invisible to the suite.

[ADVISORY] The retained "is false if embeddable_host is blank" test no longer establishes or isolates host blankness — its setup moved into the nested describe, so it passes because `embed_truncate` is false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unbuilt topic — and no test asserts the actual behavior change (expandable_first_post? is now true with zero embeddable hosts once embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? hold). A regression that reintroduces a host-existence gate in expandable_first_post? ships green: every test in this block either fabricates a host or is false for unrelated reasons, so the removed condition's new behavior is asserted nowhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional `:port` suffix (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`), and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does **not** strip the port, so a saved record can be `example.com:8080`. However, authorization uses `record_for_host(host)` which parses the referer with `URI(host).host` and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. `URI(...).host` excludes the port, so it will look for `example.com` and never match a stored `example.com:8080`, causing `host_allowed?` to always fail for port-qualified saved hosts. Additionally, if an admin enters `http://example.com:8080`, the callback strips scheme to `example.com:8080`, making this failure likely. This is directly exercised by the embed check change (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The validation regex requires a dotted domain with an alphabetic TLD, rejecting IP literals and single-label names like 'localhost' that the old setting matcher accepted (URI(h).host rescue h compared them directly against the referer host). A migrated IP or single-label host keeps working until an admin edits it — then even a category-only change fails validation with no way to re-save, and such hosts can never be re-added via the UI or API.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` (requires a dotted name + alphabetic TLD), which will reject single-label hosts like `localhost` and IP literals that the previous `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` logic would have allowed by directly comparing entries against `uri.host` (see removed logic in `app/models/site_setting.rb`). The migration inserts prior values via raw SQL (bypassing validation/callbacks), so such hosts can exist and continue to authorize embeds via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, but any admin edit/save will run validations in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` and fail even for category-only changes because it reassigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and calls `host.save`.

The updated spec includes `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` but it no longer sets `embed_truncate` true or `has_topic_embed?` true, so it passes for unrelated default reasons and does not exercise the host-related behavior. Whether keeping expansion enabled for already-embedded topics after deleting all hosts is a product decision, but the diff-grounded issue (logic gate removal + non-covering test) is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable now issues a database query (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? → WHERE lower(host) = ?) on every embed request, replacing an in-memory cached SiteSetting check, and host has no index (which lower(host) would defeat anyway). Every iframe embed request — externally embedded pages, often a site's highest-traffic surface — pays a new per-request sequential scan that the previous implementation served from memory.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` to call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), which calls `record_for_host` and performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). This is a DB query per embed request, whereas the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` used an in-memory string setting (app/models/site_setting.rb removed). The new migration creates `embeddable_hosts` without any index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), so lookups can degrade as the table grows; additionally `lower(host)` would require a functional index to be efficiently indexed. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable now runs an uncached SQL query on every request (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` → `where("lower(host) = ?").first`, unindexed on `lower(host)`), replacing a check that previously read an in-memory site setting. Every /embed/comments and /embed/count request — one per article page-view iframe for forums using embedding — now pays a per-request query plus ActiveRecord instantiation (`record_for_host` returns `.first` where `exists?` would suffice) on one of the highest-traffic endpoints, with no caching layer in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` from checking `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), i.e., a DB query plus AR object instantiation on each request. The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` adds no index on `host` or `lower(host)` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), so the concern about unindexed `lower(host)` and per-request querying is grounded. This is a performance/architecture issue rather than a functional defect verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration unconditionally indexes [0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup query, which returns zero rows for any site that never set the embed_category site setting (the default is '' and default settings are not persisted), so the migration crashes. db:migrate aborts at the migration step (NoMethodError on nil['id'] or IndexError from the result object, depending on the adapter result type) and blocks the deploy for the majority of sites; the intended fallback to uncategorized_category_id at lines 14-16 is unreachable because the crash happens before category_id == 0 is ever evaluated, and line 15 repeats the same unsafe [0]['value'] indexing.

[BUG] The backfill guard `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is dead code: cmd_tuples is always 0 for SELECT statements in PostgreSQL (PQcmdTuples returns '' for non-DML commands, which the pg gem converts to 0), so the guarded INSERT loop never runs. The unconditional `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` at line 31 then destroys every site's configured host allowlist and embed category with no replacement rows created: after deploy EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? returns false for every referer, ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess for all embed requests, TopicEmbed.import falls back to nil category, and the old configuration is unrecoverable without a database backup — silent data loss paired with a site-wide embedding outage.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration does `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and then gates the backfill with `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. For PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` is not a reliable way to check whether a SELECT returned rows (it is typically 0/blank for non-DML), so this guard can prevent the INSERT loop from ever running even when the SELECT returns a row. The migration then unconditionally executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would delete the prior configuration without creating replacement `embeddable_hosts` rows—i.e., potential silent data loss and broken embedding behavior after deploy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backfill INSERT writes each raw setting entry verbatim via unescaped string interpolation ('#{h}'), bypassing the EmbeddableHost model's before_validation stripping of scheme/path, its format validation, and parameterized escaping. Setting values the old matcher explicitly accepted (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com', 'https://example.com/1234' per the updated embed_controller_spec) would be stored un-normalized and then never match record_for_host's `lower(host) = 'eviltrout.com'` comparison, so those hosts silently stop allowing embeds even once the backfill runs; a stored value containing a single quote raises a SQL syntax error that aborts the migration.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the backfill does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, which (a) interpolates unescaped user-configured data directly into SQL (a single quote in `h` will break the migration / is unsafe), and (b) inserts the raw setting value without going through `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Since later checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, any migrated rows containing `http://...` or `/path` would not match `uri.host` and embeds would be incorrectly rejected after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true drops the table if it already exists, making this shipped migration destructive on re-run. Any execution against a database that already contains the table (schema_migrations drift after a backup restore, db:migrate:redo, or a manual re-run) silently drops the table with all admin-entered hosts and recreates it empty, with no warning and no backup step.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which (in ActiveRecord) will DROP the table if it already exists before recreating it. While migrations normally run once, any scenario that re-runs this migration (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, schema_migrations drift, manual re-run) would delete all existing `embeddable_hosts` records and recreate an empty table, matching the finding’s data-loss concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The destructive DELETE of the site_settings rows sits inside `def change`, whose raw execute calls have no inverse, so the migration cannot be rolled back. db:rollback / db:migrate:down raises ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration, and even a hand-written down method could not restore the deleted embeddable_hosts/embed_category values — once applied, the pre-migration configuration is unrecoverable except from a backup.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` defines only `def change` and performs non-reversible data operations via raw `execute`, including `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ...` and especially `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot infer an inverse for these `execute` statements, so `db:rollback` / `migrate:down` will be irreversible (or at minimum will not restore the deleted site_settings rows/values). The finding’s claim about unrecoverable pre-migration configuration is grounded in the explicit DELETE in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Deleting the embeddable_hosts/embed_category setting rows in the same release that switches every reader to the new table is an expand+contract violation with no dual-read window. During a rolling deploy, pods still running the previous code call SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? / read SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, find the rows already deleted, and reject every embed request with InvalidAccess until each pod is restarted — operators get an embedding outage whose duration equals the rolling-restart window.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. In this same diff, runtime code switches reads to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`) and removes `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` plus the `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings. During a rolling deploy, any old app instances still running pre-change code would continue to read `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` / call `allows_embeddable_host?`; after the migration deletes those rows, `embeddable_hosts` would be blank/nil for them, causing them to reject all embed requests with `InvalidAccess` until those instances are restarted. This is a real expand/contract (dual-read) deployment correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids (without include: true) emits only embeddable_host_ids and no embeddable_hosts collection anywhere in the payload, so the client store receives no host records to hydrate and embedding.embeddable_hosts cannot contain records carrying host or category data. On the admin embedding page the store's _hydrateEmbedded resolves each id via _lookupSubType against a root collection that does not exist, yielding bare/undefined entries: the table renders rows with blank host names and no category, edit() seeds the host field and category chooser from undefined, and saving such a row submits a blank category_id which save_host silently replaces with the uncategorized category.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb` the relationship is declared as `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` with no `include: true`. Given the client-side store logic in this diff, `_hydrateEmbedded` now explicitly hydrates `*_ids` arrays by looking up each id in a sideloaded root collection via `_lookupSubType` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`). If the embedding payload only contains `embeddable_host_ids` and does not also sideload an `embeddable_hosts` collection, hydration will yield `null/undefined` entries (the code even sets the pluralized key to the mapped array regardless), and the admin template iterating `embedding.embeddable_hosts` (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) would render blank rows / break actions that assume `host` is a real record. The diff does not show any other mechanism that would guarantee sideloading `embeddable_hosts`, so this is a plausible real defect stemming from the serializer configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] show renders the singleton under the singular root key 'embedding', but the route loads it with store.find('embedding') (no id), which the store routes to findAll, and findAll extracts the collection from the plural root key ('embeddings' — the shape the fruit findAll fixture added in this diff exercises), so the model load resolves to nothing or garbage. The admin embedding page's model never becomes the expected record: the host table never renders ({{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}} stays falsy) and the Add Host button throws on undefined.pushObject, leaving the PR's primary screen dead for admins.

adjudication.rationale: The admin route’s model hook calls `this.store.find('embedding')` with no id (app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6). In this codebase’s store/REST conventions (reinforced by the updated store tests/fixtures: singular root for `find(type,id)` vs plural for `findAll(type)`), an id-less `find` is liable to behave like a collection load and expect a plural root (e.g. `embeddings`). But the server endpoint added is a singleton `show` at `/admin/customize/embedding` that renders under the singular root key `embedding` (Admin::EmbeddingController#show + EmbeddingSerializer). If the store treats this as a findAll/collection response, the model would not hydrate into the expected record, making `embedding.embeddable_hosts` undefined/falsy and breaking both the table rendering and `pushObject` in `addHost`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action attaches only .then to destroyRecord() with no rejection handler, unlike save() which pairs its promise with .catch(popupAjaxError), so a failed host deletion produces no error surface at all. When the DELETE fails (network error, or the 500 the destroy action returns for an already-deleted id on a double-delete), the admin gets no popup and no indication of failure — the row silently remains in the table and the operation looks like it did nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but never attaches a rejection handler (unlike `save()`, which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE fails, the UI provides no error feedback and the host is not removed (because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `.then`). This is especially plausible given `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy` does `host = ...first; host.destroy` without a nil check, so a missing/already-deleted id would raise and return a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy looks the host up with where(id: params[:id]).first and calls host.destroy without a nil check, so an id that matches no record raises NoMethodError and the endpoint returns a raw 500 instead of a 404 or an idempotent success. A stale tab or a double-confirmed delete issues a second DELETE for an already-destroyed id: the server 500s, and because the component's delete promise has no catch the admin sees nothing — the failure is completely invisible and the row's fate is ambiguous.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, both `destroy` and `update` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on `host` (`host.destroy` in `destroy`, and `save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`), with no nil check. If the id is missing/already deleted, this will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500. On the client side, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` `delete()` calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(...)`, so such a server failure would be silent in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update passes a nil host into save_host when params[:id] matches no record, and save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] unguarded, so both a stale id and a missing param envelope crash with NoMethodError (host.host= on nil) and return a 500 where a 404/400 belongs. PUT/POST /admin/embeddable_hosts with an unknown id or without the embeddable_host envelope yields an opaque 500 with no validation feedback; API consumers cannot distinguish 'bad request' from 'server broken' and the record is silently left unsaved.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record matches, `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately calls `host.host = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 instead of a 404. Separately, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without guarding against a missing `embeddable_host` envelope, which would also raise and return a 500. Both issues are directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! unguarded, so saving an EmbeddableHost whose host attribute is nil (create/update with embeddable_host params that omit :host) raises NoMethodError inside the callback instead of failing the format validation. A request omitting the host key returns a 500 from nil.sub! rather than the validation 4xx that render_json_error would produce, turning a client input error into an apparent server fault.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` will set `host` to nil if the client omits `:host` (or `params[:embeddable_host]` lacks that key). With `host` nil, `sub!` raises `NoMethodError` before validations run, producing a 500 instead of a validation error path (`render_json_error(host)`). The migration’s `null: false` constraint doesn’t prevent this runtime error because it occurs before hitting the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The validation regex explicitly accepts a :port suffix and before_validation preserves it, but record_for_host matches only uri.host (port stripped), so a saved host-with-port can never equal any referer's host and never authorizes embedding. An admin who saves 'example.com:8080' gets a success response and a table row, yet every embed request from that host fails EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? with Discourse::InvalidAccess — the configuration silently never works and nothing tells the admin the saved value is unusable.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the host format validation explicitly allows an optional ":port" suffix (/:([0-9]{1,5})?/), and the before_validation callback strips protocol and path but does not remove the port (it only does sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '') and sub!(/\/.*$/, '')). However, record_for_host parses the referer/embed URL via URI(...) and then compares using uri.host (port stripped) against the DB value: where("lower(host) = ?", host). So a stored value like "example.com:8080" will never match incoming requests from "http://example.com:8080/..." because uri.host is "example.com". This makes such a configuration silently non-functional, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] saveChanges fires embedding.update({}) as a dropped promise (no .then/.catch) against an update endpoint that persists nothing — Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders the current state — and no template in this diff wires the action to any button. The next maintainer who wires this action up (the method name and the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route advertise a save) ships a button that reports success while saving nothing, and a failed PUT is swallowed without any error surfaced to the user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an Ember controller action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` without any `.then/.catch` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), and it also adds a PUT route/controller action `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` that does not persist anything and simply re-serializes the current `@embedding` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb). Additionally, the new `embedding.hbs` template wires only `addHost`/`deleteHost` and contains no button invoking `saveChanges`. So it’s not a user-facing broken behavior in this diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/footgun issue: the presence of a “save” action and PUT endpoint suggests saving should occur while it currently does not and errors would be unhandled if wired up later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new plural hydration branch drops the singular branch's falsy guard and calls obj[k].map unguarded: a payload key like xxx_ids present with a null value throws a TypeError inside hydration and rejects the whole find, while ids not resolvable from the root collection silently become undefined entries in the hydrated relation (the trailing 'hydrated || []' is dead code because map always returns an array). Shared store infrastructure now turns a null *_ids payload into a hard failure of every find of that type and turns unresolvable ids into undefined records that surface downstream as blank/broken components instead of a skipped entry or an error.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was changed to also hydrate plural `*_ids` keys via `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` when the regex matches the optional `s` (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`). This new branch does not guard against `obj[k]` being `null`/`undefined`, so a payload like `{ color_ids: null }` will throw a `TypeError` on `.map` and break the whole hydration/find. Additionally, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`, and the code pushes those into the resulting array, yielding relations with `undefined` entries; the `hydrated || []` is ineffective since `.map` always returns an array. These behaviors are directly introduced by the diff and can cause hard failures or downstream broken components.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration deletes the 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' site_settings rows while not-yet-restarted app servers in a rolling deploy still run the old code that gates every embed request on SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, which now falls back to its blank default. On multi-server installs, embed requests 403 intermittently (on each server not yet restarted since the migration ran) even though the new admin UI shows the hosts configured — a silent per-node feature outage during the deploy window.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, and this diff also removes the corresponding settings from `config/site_settings.yml` / `server.en.yml`. While the new runtime code paths (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, `TopicEmbed.import`) no longer consult `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category`, the diff itself makes it clear that older app servers (still running pre-change code during a rolling deploy) would continue to gate embeds on `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` and could fail once the rows are deleted. This is a real deploy/backward-compatibility concern grounded in the migration, but not a defect in the post-deploy code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fabricator definitions are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the newly added embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds all of the category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category definitions. Contributors looking for the category fabricators open category_fabricator.rb and find an embeddable-host fabricator; the misfiled definitions invite duplicate fabricators and conflicting edits the next time either area changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the category fabricators were moved out of `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` (it now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` definitions.
